Cd also disrupts trafficking, autophagosome-lysosome fusion, lysosomal integrity and proteolysis, providing stronger evidence for incomplete bulk autophagic processing than for mitochondria-specific stalled flux. Among the compounds examined, puerarin has the broadest checkpoint coverage, largely from related cortical studies, linking reduced Cd burden and mitochondrial stress with pool preservation and improved bulk autophagic processing. Evidence for daidzein remains marker-limited, whereas Rg1 protects neuronal and glial endpoints without an established Cd-specific mitochondrial quality-control mechanism. This narrative, non-systematic synthesis is limited by potential selection bias, reliance on static markers, dominance of acute or high-dose exposure models, limited measurement of mitochondria-specific degradation and replacement, inadequate cell-type resolution and scarce independent replication. Resolving these states requires mitochondria-specific flux reporters, direct degradation and replacement indices, causal pathway perturbation and matched Cd and compound exposure. Therapeutic benefit is more likely to arise from restoring selective, proportionate and completed mitochondrial turnover balanced by replacement than from uniformly activating or suppressing mitophagy.

article.title: Structural Social Connection, Biological Ageing, and Neurodegenerative Disease Burden: A Global Ecological Analysis of Household Size and Modelled Dementia Incidence Estimates.
article.authors: Wenpeng You
article.abstract: BACKGROUND: Poor social connection and ageing-related biological processes are recognised contributors to Alzheimer's disease and related dementias. However, cross-national evidence linking structural indicators of social connection with dementia and broader neurological dis-ease burden remains limited. This ecological study examined country-level associations be-tween average household size and modelled neurological disease incidence estimates. METHODS: Country- and territory-level data from up to 204 settings were analysed. Average household size was the primary exposure, and model-derived, age-standardised incidence-rate estimates for Alzheimer's disease and other dementias were the primary outcome. Par-kinson's disease, motor neuron disease, multiple sclerosis, idiopathic epilepsy, headache dis-orders, and total neurological disorders were examined as comparative secondary outcomes. The Henneberg Index, life expectancy at age 60, GDP per capita, and urban living were in-cluded as contextual covariates. Analyses included Pearson and Spearman correlations, par-tial correlations, principal component analysis, and multivariable linear regression. RESULTS: Household size was strongly and inversely associated with Alzheimer's disease and other dementias incidence estimates (Pearson r=-.841, p<.001). The association remained after adjustment for the included covariates (β=-.569, p<.001). Significant inverse adjusted associations were also observed for Parkinson's disease, motor neuron disease, and total neurological disorders, whereas patterns differed for other neurological outcomes. Principal component analysis identified a single ageing-development dimension explaining 72.1% of the variance, with household size loading inversely against life expectancy at age 60, econom-ic affluence, urban living, and the Henneberg Index. CONCLUSION: Smaller average household size was associated with higher modelled incidence estimates for dementia and selected neurodegenerative diseases at the country level. These findings should be interpreted as ecological associations rather than evidence of individual-level causation and suggest that household structure is embedded within broader demograph-ic, socioeconomic, and ageing-related processes.

article.title: Genomic profiling of estrogen-related receptor identifies adult adipocyte-specific targets in Drosophila.
article.authors: Jun Yin; Douglas B Rusch; Jitika S Bhatta; David M Merritt; Lesley N Weaver
article.abstract: Adipose tissue is a key metabolic organ for carbohydrate and lipid metabolism. Multiple nutrient sensing pathways and metabolic enzymes operate in adipocytes to control energy production and lipid mobilization in response to physiological conditions. Important regulators of glycolytic and lipid metabolism in many species are members of the estrogen-related receptor (ERR) family of nuclear receptors. We previously showed that ERR is required for transcriptional regulation of glycolytic and pentose phosphate pathway enzymes in adult Drosophila females, consistent with what is observed in ERR mutant males and larvae. However, the cell-type specific targets of ERR in adipose and other tissues have not been fully elucidated. Here, using a modified targeted DamID approach (NanoDam), we identified ERR occupancy specifically in adult adipocytes at the loci that encode genes involved in glycolysis, the pentose phosphate pathway, and fatty acid metabolism. Overall, our results predict that ERR centrally functions in adipose tissue to regulate multiple metabolic pathways.

article.title: CDH1 loss remodels gene expression and lineage identity in human mammary epithelial cells.
article.authors: Maggie Musick; Chinasa A Ufondu; Carmen E Rowland; Micaela E Brown; Joseph L Sottnik; Madeleine T Shackleford; Camryn S Nesiba; Etienne P Danis; Andrew E Goodspeed; Richard Zera; Arthur T Johnson; Kathryn L Schwertfeger; Andrew C Nelson; Julie H Ostrander; Matthew J Sikora
article.abstract: Invasive lobular carcinoma (ILC) is a common subtype of breast cancer, molecularly defined by genetic loss of CDH1, and subsequent loss of cell adhesion protein E-cadherin, in ~95% of ILC. Though CDH1 loss occurs early in ILC oncogenesis, it is unclear how this facilitates transformation. We modeled early CDH1 loss using "normal" human mammary epithelial cells (HMEC), i.e., finite lifespan cells reflecting early hyperplasia, and targeted E-cadherin signaling using antibodies versus causing genetic CDH1 loss using siRNA or CRISPR/Cas9-knockout. Transcriptome analysis across four HMEC models showed that the mode of E-cadherin targeting is critical for the subsequent phenotype. Antibody-mediated inhibition of cell-cell contacts induced gene signatures of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), consistent with the role of E-cadherin suppression during the EMT process. Conversely, genetic CDH1 loss - as in ILC oncogenesis - repressed EMT signatures, and instead remodeled gene expression toward a luminal epithelial phenotype. RNA-seq, single cell transcriptomics, flow cytometry, microscopy, and ATAC-seq analyses support that CDH1 loss induces lineage remodeling to a luminal state, which is mirrored in transcriptomic analysis of clinical ILC precursor lesions. By isolating luminal versus basal cells prior to CDH1 knockout, we found that CDH1 loss led to remodeling of lineage identity in both populations, converging on a new lineage homeostasis with a luminal progenitor-like phenotype. Consistent with the shift to a luminal progenitor phenotype, CDH1 loss enhanced proliferative capacity over the finite lifespan of the HMECs, highlighting a feature of early CDH1 loss that may contribute to clonal advantage during tumor initiation. Moreover, CDH1 loss enhanced anoikis resistance, a defining feature of ILC cells. Our findings support that genetic loss of CDH1 in mammary epithelial cells induces transcriptional and phenotypic changes consistent with lineage identity remodeling toward a luminal progenitor-like state, which may underpin the mechanism by which early CDH1 loss mediates ILC oncogenesis.

article.title: SIRT5 deficiency exacerbates sepsis acute renal injury by activating ACSL4/FTH1 axis dependent ferroptosis.
article.authors: Liliang Jiang; Xi Yu; Guang Shan; Ziqi He; Yongbo Liu; Wenlong Lin; Lingling Song; Zhongyuan Xia
article.abstract: Sepsis‑associated acute kidney injury (S‑AKI) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in critically ill patients, yet effective targeted therapies remain lacking due to an incomplete understanding of its pathogenesis. Ferroptosis, an iron‑dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, has recently been implicated in AKI, but the upstream regulators of this process in sepsis remain undefined. Here, we identify SIRT5, a mitochondrial NAD ⁺ ‑dependent desuccinylase, as a critical endogenous suppressor of ferroptosis in S‑AKI. Using a cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) murine model and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)‑stimulated HK‑2 proximal tubular cells, we show that SIRT5 expression is significantly downregulated in septic kidney injury. Renal tubular‑specific ablation of Sirt5 exacerbated CLP‑induced renal dysfunction, structural damage, and tubular cell death, whereas AAV9‑mediated SIRT5 overexpression attenuated these pathological changes. Mechanistically, SIRT5 deficiency tipped the balance of the ACSL4/FTH1 axis toward ferroptosis: it increased ACSL4‑dependent membrane lipid remodeling and reduced FTH1‑mediated iron sequestration, accompanied by suppression of the antioxidant enzyme GPX4. Consequently, lipid peroxidation, iron overload, and mitochondrial damage were markedly amplified. Notably, knockdown of ACSL4 in SIRT5‑deficient HK‑2 cells effectively reversed lipid peroxidation, iron accumulation, and cell death, establishing ACSL4 as a key downstream effector of SIRT5‑mediated ferroptosis suppression. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized SIRT5-ACSL4/FTH1 regulatory axis that governs ferroptotic susceptibility in renal tubular cells during sepsis, and suggest that pharmacological restoration of SIRT5 activity or blockade of ACSL4‑driven ferroptosis may offer novel therapeutic avenues for S‑AKI.

article.title: Mesothelin-induced lysosomal biogenesis sustains neutrophil longevity to drive brain metastasis.
article.authors: Xiaoxia Chen; Chengtao Dong; Yinglun Wang; Tianyu Yun; Li Wang; Ruizhe Chen; Yuchen Shen; Caiting Tang; Yuxuan Xie; Kunlin Zeng; Yong Yang; Zelong Han; Junguo Bu; Shangbiao Li; Aidong Zhou
article.abstract: Tumor-associated neutrophil (TAN) enrichment is a defining feature and driving force of brain metastases (BrMs), a leading cause of death in solid tumors. Yet, the mechanisms governing TAN enrichment in BrM remains undefined. Herein, we demonstrate that BrM cell-derived shed soluble mesothelin (sMSLN) critically prolongs neutrophil survival to facilitate tumor cell colonization and outgrowth in the brain. Specifically, sMSLN binds to toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) on neutrophil to activate the JAK2-STAT3 pathway. This activation promotes lysosomal biogenesis and function, reducing cellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and inhibiting neutrophil apoptosis. Neutrophil depletion or TLR4-STAT3 blockade abrogates sMSLN-induced BrM progression. Targeting MSLN with Anetumab effectively reduces TAN enrichment, and combining this with TLR4 inhibition synergistically suppresses lung cancer BrM. Our findings establish a critical role for tumor cell-derived sMSLN in sustaining neutrophil longevity and driving BrM, highlighting the sMSLN-TLR4 axis as a promising therapeutic target for brain metastatic tumors.

article.title: Sonic hedgehog-matrix metalloproteinase crosstalk in neurovascular ageing and stroke: a potential mechanistic link.
article.authors: Priya Bindal; Paul R Kasher; Satoshi Ogawa
article.abstract: Neurovascular ageing is a major contributor to cerebrovascular vulnerability and poor stroke outcomes in older adults. Progressive deterioration of the neurovascular unit (NVU), driven by oxidative stress, neurovascular coupling dysfunction, blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption, inflammageing, cellular senescence, mitochondrial dysfunction, and impaired autophagy compromises neurovascular resilience and increases susceptibility to ischemic injury. Among the molecular pathways implicated in these processes, Sonic hedgehog (Shh) signaling and matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs) are important regulators of neurovascular remodeling, BBB integrity, and post-stroke recovery. Although these pathways have largely been investigated independently, emerging evidence suggests potential bidirectional interactions between Shh signaling and MMP activity. In particular, Shh/Gli1 signaling has been associated with regulation of MMP-2 and MMP-9 in experimental models, whereas MMP-2 can disrupt SCUBE2, an extracellular regulator of Shh ligand presentation, providing a potential mechanism for reciprocal pathway modulation. This review examines the Shh-MMP axis as a potential mechanistic link between neurovascular ageing and ischemic vulnerability, integrating current evidence to evaluate how dysregulation of these pathways may contribute to BBB dysfunction, extracellular matrix remodeling, neuroinflammation, and impaired neurovascular repair. We further discuss the potential therapeutic implications of modulating the Shh-MMP axis to preserve neurovascular resilience and improve cerebrovascular outcomes in the ageing brain, while highlighting the importance of temporal and cell-specific targeting.

article.title: Therapeutic effect of quercetin on airway remodeling of ovalbumin-induced asthmatic mice via inhibition of the mtDNA-cGAS-STING pathway.
article.authors: Rihuang Qiu; Zhiwen Liu; Pingkang Li; Laishui Peng; Yuhui Xu; Yiming Zeng
article.abstract: Asthma is a chronic inflammatory airway disease with limited treatments for airway remodeling. Quercetin has anti-inflammatory potential, but whether it acts through the mtDNA-cGAS-STING pathway remains unclear. This study aimed to explore the therapeutic effect of quercetin on asthma in a mouse model and the associated underlying molecular mechanism. Various doses of quercetin were employed to intervene in a mouse model of asthma. Alterations in inflammation-related indicators and mtDNA in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF), pathological changes in lung tissue, and activation of the cGAS-STING signaling pathway were detected. The STING agonist DMXAA was utilized to verify whether quercetin could enhance the relevant indicators in the mouse asthma model by suppressing the activation of the mtDNA-cGAS-STING signaling pathway. Finally, BEAS-2B cells were treated with TGF-β to mimic the epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) process of asthmatic epithelial cells. Quercetin, a STING overexpression vector and ethidium bromide intervention were used to analyze whether quercetin inhibited the TGF-β-induced EMT process in BEAS-2B cells by suppressing the mtDNA-cGAS-STING signaling pathway. Quercetin treatment effectively mitigated inflammatory infiltration and airway remodeling in a mouse model of asthma, and the therapeutic effect was most pronounced at a high dose. Additionally, quercetin treatment inhibited the activation of the mtDNA-cGAS-STING signaling pathway in asthmatic mice. Treatment with DMXAA reversed the therapeutic effect of quercetin in the mouse model of asthma. At the cellular level, quercetin inhibited TGF-β-induced EMT in BEAS-2B cells by suppressing the mtDNA-cGAS-STING signaling pathway. Thus, quercetin can ameliorate inflammatory infiltration and airway remodeling in a mouse model of asthma, potentially by suppressing the activation of the mtDNA-cGAS-STING signaling pathway.

article.title: Glycated albumin levels in roe deer: a marker of body condition modulated by environmental quality.
article.authors: Cyrielle Duval; Benjamin Rey; Jean-François Lemaître; Emmanuelle Gilot-Fromont; Jean-Michel Gaillard; Maryline Pellerin; Sarahi Jaramillo-Ortiz; Christine Schaeffer-Reiss; Fabrice Bertile; François Criscuolo
article.abstract: In humans, it is now widely accepted that the glycation reaction plays a major role in the senescence process, as well as in the development of associated pathologies. While the links between glycation and senescence have also been studied in laboratory animal models, they have hardly been studied in the wild. We therefore investigated the links between glycation and senescence in two populations of roe deer (Capreolus capreolus) facing different environmental conditions, in which demographic and phenotypic senescence are well documented. Individuals of known age were captured in two years of differing quality. Individual data were collected (body mass, glycemia, sex), and we measured glycated albumin levels (GA) as well as six biochemical parameters known to show senescence in this species. We found that GA did not correlate with age, blood glucose, or sex, but varied between populations and years. In the population living in the low-quality environment, GA was negatively associated with inflammatory status while GA was positively associated with body mass. Overall, GA appears to reflect aspects of physiological condition and individual performance in an environment-dependent context, rather than senescence.

article.title: Neuroinflammation in levodopa-induced dyskinesia in Parkinson's disease: current state of the art.
article.authors: Bruno Lopes Santos-Lobato; Tatiane Piedade de Souza Machado; Luiz Vinicius Silva Correa; Margarete Zanardo Gomes; Elaine A Del-Bel; Vitor Tumas
article.abstract: Levodopa-induced dyskinesia (LID) remains a major limitation of long-term dopaminergic therapy in Parkinson's disease (PD). Although LID is classically attributed to maladaptive corticostriatal plasticity driven by pulsatile dopaminergic stimulation in the dopamine-denervated striatum, accumulating evidence indicates that chronic neuroinflammation may lower the threshold for LID development and expression. Here, we synthesize preclinical, human biomarkers, neuroimaging, and genetic findings that support neuroinflammation as a mechanistic bridge between cellular stress and circuit-level maladaptation. In animal models, pharmacological modulation of inflammation-linked pathways, particularly nitrergic signaling, antibiotic repurposing, and cannabinoid-based strategies, attenuates abnormal involuntary movements and reduces striatal glial reactivity, implicating an inflammation-plasticity coupling in LID. In humans, post-mortem studies implicate regionally constrained mitochondrial DNA abnormalities and lipid dysregulation in the striatum, while biofluid metabolomics supports altered nitric oxide generation and lipid pathways associated with LID severity. Neuroimaging studies reveal markers consistent with oxidative stress and neurovascular dysfunction, and genetic studies link LID risk to variants in genes involved in lysosomal function, mitochondrial homeostasis, and inflammatory transcriptional programs. Integrated with the classic mechanisms of LID pathophysiology, we propose a conceptual model organized around three interrelated dimensions: (i) the topographical distribution of neuroinflammatory changes, particularly within the striatum; (ii) the interaction of neuroinflammation with mitochondrial dysfunction and lipid dysregulation; and (iii) the modifying influence of genetic susceptibility. This model motivates biomarker-guided, randomized trials targeting specific inflammatory nodes to prevent or mitigate LID.

article.title: Enzymatic In Situ Self-Assembly of a Fluorogenic Photosensitizer Induces PANoptosis for Photodynamic-Immunotherapy.
article.authors: Yuyang Tian; Pengke Zhao; Mengxian Ling; Yinxing Miao; Yili Liu; Jian He; Jing-Juan Xu; Yan Zhang; Jiewei Luo; Deju Ye
article.abstract: PANoptosis, an inflammatory programmed cell death that integrates pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis, holds great promise for cancer immunotherapy. However, conventional strategies relying on PANoptosome assembly are hindered by complex upstream signaling requirements. Here, we report P-CHD-TPP, an enzyme-instructed in situ self-assembling probe that triggers PANoptosome-independent PANoptosis via persistent mitochondrial disruption. Upon alkaline phosphatase (ALP)-triggered dephosphorylation, P-CHD-TPP self-assembles into fluorescent nanoparticles decorated with triphenylphosphonium (TPP) and 1,3-cyclohexanedione (CHD) groups, which are rapidly internalized by tumor cells and preferentially accumulate in mitochondria. The TPP groups in the assembled nanoparticles moderately disrupt mitochondrial homeostasis, leading to protein sulfenylation. Then, the CHD moiety covalently labels and inactivates these sulfenylated proteins, effectively disabling the endogenous reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging system. Upon near-infrared irradiation, a massive ROS burst is generated, inflicting severe and sustained mitochondrial damage. This cascade induces rapid PANoptosis-associated pathways and triggers profound mitochondrial DNA release to activate the cGAS-STING pathway. The combined activation elicits robust antitumor immunity, effectively suppressing orthotopic 4T1 tumor growth and prolonging survival. This work establishes a mitochondrial sulfenylated protein-labeling strategy that amplifies oxidative stress, providing a paradigm for PANoptosis-based photodynamic-immunotherapy.

article.title: Evaluation of antibacterial activity of hydroethanolic seed extract of Descurainia sophia against multidrug-resistant Salmonella typhi isolated from typhoid patients: an integrated in silico and in vitro study.
article.authors: Malaiqa Qureshi; Raim Fatima; Ahsan Anjum; Bukhtawar Khan; Muhammad Imran Ali Khan; Abdul Rehman; Maliha Khalid Khan; Imran Ahmad Khan; Hafiza Hamed
article.venue: International microbiology : the official journal of the Spanish Society for Microbiology
article.abstract: Typhoid fever caused by Salmonella typhi remains a major public health problem, and multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant strains have left few oral treatment options in endemic regions such as Pakistan. Seeds of Descurainia sophia (L.) are used in Unani and folk medicine for febrile illness and contain cardenolides, glucosinolate-derived isothiocyanates and long-chain fatty acids, but their activity against MDR S. typhi and a plausible molecular target have not been examined. We therefore combined in silico and in vitro approaches to evaluate a hydroethanolic seed extract against clinical MDR S. typhi isolates. A library of 14 literature-reported seed compounds was screened by ADMET profiling (admetSAR 3.0), which selected three drug-like cardenolides (helveticoside, evomonoside and strophanthidin); these were docked against DNA gyrase A with moxifloxacin and gemifloxacin as references, and the top-ranked lead, helveticoside, was then examined in a 50 ns all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulation. The extract was characterised by GC-MS and FTIR and tested against five MDR isolates (MDR-ST1 to MDR-ST5) by disc diffusion and broth microdilution (CLSI M07). GC-MS confirmed 13 of the 14 library compounds (91.4% of total ion chromatogram area), including the three leads; erysimoside was the only compound not detected. Helveticoside (- 9.7 kcal/mol) and evomonoside (- 9.5) showed higher predicted affinities than moxifloxacin (- 7.9) and gemifloxacin (- 8.2); strophanthidin scored - 8.5. In the MD simulation, the helveticoside complex remained stable (ligand RMSD ~ 1.8 Å without dissociation; protein Cα RMSD ~ 2.2-2.5 Å after ~ 15 ns), and 12 residues, including ARG31, SER185 and GLN288, contacted the ligand in > 95% of frames, six of them also present in the docked pose. The extract inhibited all five isolates in a dose-dependent manner (mean zone of inhibition 11.5-17.15 mm at 25-100 mg/mL; 19.3 ± 0.9 mm for moxifloxacin, reported descriptively because the extract is crude), with a geometric mean MIC of 8.4 mg/mL (range 6.25-12.5) and MBC/MIC = 2 for all isolates, consistent with bactericidal activity. FTIR showed functional groups consistent with the major constituent classes.Docking and MD together generate the hypothesis that DNA gyrase A inhibition by cardenolide constituents may contribute to the antibacterial effect of the extract. The MD simulation supports the structural stability of the predicted helveticoside binding mode but does not demonstrate enzyme inhibition, and fatty acids and isothiocyanates in the extract may also contribute. Overall, the crude extract showed in vitro antibacterial activity against MDR S. typhi at high concentrations, and the study provides a testable mechanistic hypothesis that requires bioactivity-guided fractionation, pure-compound testing and target-engagement assays.

article.title: Neurotropic herpesviruses as accelerators of brain aging: The role of latency and reactivation in neurodegeneration.
article.authors: Pooja Nadholta; Ipsita Volety; Deepak Shukla
article.abstract: Neurotropic herpesviruses establish lifelong latency within the human nervous system. Traditionally viewed as either harmless latent infections or rare causes of acute encephalitis, growing evidence suggests these viruses undergo recurrent, subclinical reactivations throughout life. This review summarizes recent advances and introduces the multiple-hit viral reactivation model, proposing that repeated silent reactivation events act as cumulative biological stressors that accelerate brain aging. We describe a self-reinforcing cycle in which age-related immunosenescence impairs control of viral latency, leading to recurrent subclinical reactivation, chronic neuroinflammation, cellular senescence, and progressive disruption of central nervous system homeostasis. Rather than directly causing neurodegenerative disease, recurrent host-virus interactions gradually diminish brain resilience and promote the accumulation of pathogenic protein aggregates, including amyloid-β, tau, α-synuclein, and TDP-43. Clinical neurodegeneration emerges when the cumulative burden of lifelong viral reactivation exceeds the aging brain's capacity to maintain homeostasis. Recognizing herpesviruses as modifiable drivers of brain aging identifies subclinical viral reactivation as a key therapeutic target for preventing cognitive decline.

article.title: Drp1-mediated mitochondrial fission contributes to ox-LDL-induced phenotypic transition and calcification in human coronary artery smooth muscle cells.
article.authors: Zhi-Bo Fu; Yu Li; Shu-Ying Ding; Jun-Yi Luo; Xiang Ma; Zi-Xiang Yu
article.abstract: Vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) phenotypic transition is central to vascular calcification (VC), a major complication of cardiovascular disease. To investigate how oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL) drives VSMC reprogramming, we examined dynamin-related protein 1 (Drp1) in human coronary artery smooth muscle cells (HCASMCs). Three experimental series were used. Pharmacological series: control, ox-LDL, ox-LDL + Mdivi-1, ox-LDL + p38 inhibitor, and osteogenic medium as positive control. Genetic series: ox-LDL + si-NC and ox-LDL + si-Drp1. Epistasis series: si-NC, si-NC + ox-LDL, si-Drp1 + ox-LDL, and si-Drp1 + ox-LDL + anisomycin. Exposure to 25 μg/mL ox-LDL for 18 days induced phenotypic changes and calcification, with increased mineralization markers and Drp1 expression accompanied by mitochondrial fission. Runx2 was elevated, whereas SM22α and α-SMA were reduced, indicating an osteogenic shift. Drp1 inhibition attenuated mitochondrial fragmentation, phenotypic conversion, and calcification, with partial restoration of mitochondrial membrane potential (red/green ratio). p38 MAPK inhibition similarly alleviated phenotypic transition and calcification, downregulated Fis1, increased SM22α and α-SMA, and reduced Runx2. In epistasis experiments, p38 reactivation largely reversed the protective effects of Drp1 knockdown, suggesting that the effects of Drp1-dependent mitochondrial fission are mediated, at least in part, through the p38 MAPK signaling pathway, with Fis1 as a candidate further downstream node. Thus, Drp1-dependent mitochondrial fission and the p38 MAPK signaling pathway it engages are candidate entry points for further investigation in VC; in vivo validation remains necessary.

article.title: Developmental sleep during lethargus is associated with metabolic homeostasis and heritable adaptive responses to infection in Caenorhabditis elegans.
article.authors: Bynedi Seshadhri Chinna Mounish; Kannan Srilekha; Ramesh Anand; Krishnaswamy Balamurugan
article.abstract: Sleep is a fundamental physiological state essential for metabolic and neuronal homeostasis; however, its contribution to lipid and energy metabolism during development remains incompletely understood. Here, we used Caenorhabditis elegans to investigate the metabolic significance of Developmentally Timed Sleep (DTS). Lethargus-associated DTS was mechanically disrupted using 1 kHz piezoelectric buzzer-induced mechanical stimulation, followed by behavioural, physiological, metabolic and molecular analyses. DTS disruption was associated with reduced behavioural quiescence, altered sleep-associated gene expression, reduced survival and elevated oxidative stress. Notably, disruption during the L4-young adult lethargus window was associated with increased feeding and markedly enhanced lipid accumulation, accompanied by upregulation of the lipid metabolic regulators fat-6, nhr-64 and nhr-80. Despite increased lipid storage, levels of the triglyceride lipase ATGL were elevated, suggesting enhanced lipid mobilization concurrent with persistent lipid accumulation. This metabolic phenotype was accompanied by reduced mitochondrial activity, decreased intracellular ATP, downregulation of atp-3 and activation of AMPK-mediated energy sensing, suggesting energetic stress and potentially inefficient downstream utilization of mobilized lipids. DTS disruption was additionally associated with increased acy-1 and crh-1 expression and enhanced CREB phosphorylation, indicating altered cAMP-CREB-associated neuronal signalling. Furthermore, disruption of DTS in offspring of Salmonella Typhi-infected parents was associated with reduction in their ability to generate heritable adaptive resistance and altered daf-16, sgk-1 and skn-1 mRNA expression. Collectively, these findings suggest that developmental sleep may play a role in lipid storage, mobilization, mitochondrial bioenergetics and cellular energy sensing, with potential consequences for neuronal and adaptive stress responses.

article.title: Stressor-specific mitochondrial responses in bovine endometrium-derived cells reveal dissociation between oxidative burden and mitochondrial outcome.
article.authors: Maria Carolina Werner; Georg Thaller; Mohammed Saeed-Zidane
article.abstract: Inflammatory and environmental stressors can compromise uterine function and fertility. Mitochondria are central regulators of energy metabolism, redox balance, and stress adaptation; however, it remains unclear whether the magnitude of oxidative stress predicts mitochondrial outcomes in endometrium-derived cells exposed to different stress contexts. In this study, bovine endometrium-derived cells were exposed to lipopolysaccharide (LPS), hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), or heat stress (41 °C), followed by overnight recovery. Mitochondrial-associated responses were assessed by measuring intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS), MitoTracker Red fluorescence, total cellular ATP content, mitochondrial DNA copy number, and mitochondrial protein-coding gene expression. All stress conditions increased ROS levels, with the highest levels observed after H2O2 exposure. However, ROS accumulation was not consistently associated with the extent of mitochondrial alterations across stress conditions. H2O2 treatment was associated with lower MitoTracker Red fluorescence than heat stress, whereas LPS specifically reduced total cellular ATP content after recovery. Both LPS and H2O2 increased mitochondrial DNA copy number, while heat stress had no significant effect. Inflammatory stress was also associated with reduced mitochondrial respiratory chain transcript abundance, whereas oxidative and heat stress were compatible with preservation of mitochondrial transcriptional balance after recovery. These findings indicate that stressor-specific mitochondrial states may arise despite shared oxidative burden, with inflammatory stress showing the most pronounced alterations after recovery under the conditions tested.

article.title: Novel neonicotinoid flupyradifurone exhibits sublethal toxicity to natural enemies ladybeetles Propylea japonica by disturbing multi-level metabolic systems.
article.authors: Wei Li; Jiangwei Zheng; Yubing Ma; Yanrong Wu; Jie Liu; Shichang Zhang; Yao Zhao; Yu Peng
article.abstract: Flupyradifurone, a novel neonicotinoid insecticide widely used against sap-sucking pests, has poorly characterized sublethal effects on non-target natural enemies. We assessed sublethal effects of 0.5 and 3 mg/L flupyradifurone on Propylea japonica using biological, biochemical, transcriptomic, and metabolomic assays. Flupyradifurone significantly prolonged larval development and reduced adult body weight and fecundity, without affecting survival, pupation, or emergence. Enzyme activities (GST, POD and AChE) and nutritional substance contents (glycogen and free fatty acids) generally decreased at 12 and 24 h. However, CarE activity and total protein content showed no significant changes at 24 h. Transcriptomics analysis identified 1798 and 1607 differentially expressed genes, enriched in xenobiotic metabolism, immunity, and nutrient metabolism. Key genes GST, UGT, Duox, and TPS were significantly downregulated, whereas GLD was significantly upregulated, and Lys and FASN were significantly induced only at the low concentration. RNAi silencing of GST, UGT, Duox, TPS, and GLD increased ladybeetles susceptibility to flupyradifurone. Metabolomics analysis identified 483 and 508 differentially accumulated metabolites, with disruptions in glutathione, amino acid, and lipid metabolism. Thus, flupyradifurone suppresses detoxification and immunity, depletes energy reserves, and inhibits development and reproduction in P. japonica, highlighting the need to incorporate sublethal effects into ecological risk assessments.

article.title: Physiological responses of the invasive mussel Mytella strigata to atmospheric heatwaves under a simulated tidal cycle.
article.authors: Wanqing Zeng; Xinming Liang; Xin Xu; Yong Liu; Liqiang Zhao
article.abstract: Atmospheric heatwaves increasingly threaten intertidal bivalves and ecosystems they support, yet the thermal responses of the highly invasive mussel Mytella strigata remain poorly understood. In this study, mussels were exposed to a simulated tidal regime for five days, with aerial temperatures of 32 °C (control) or 40 °C (heatwave) during low tide. Transcriptomic analysis identified 2497 DEGs, including 1157 upregulated and 1340 downregulated genes. These genes were primarily enriched in protein processing in the endoplasmic reticulum, MAPK signaling, oxidative phosphorylation, and carbohydrate metabolism. Heat shock proteins and endoplasmic-reticulum quality-control genes were upregulated, indicating enhanced proteostasis maintenance. The upregulation of genes involved in the mitochondrial respiratory chain suggested an increased capacity for ATP production. Meanwhile, the differential expression of cellulase, β-glucosidase, and phosphoglucomutase indicated substantial carbohydrate metabolic remodeling. Our findings suggest that M. strigata responds to heatwave exposure through coordinated proteostasis regulation, metabolic remodeling, and antioxidant defense. Increased catalase activity accompanied by reduced malondialdehyde content suggests that antioxidant compensation effectively limited lipid peroxidation, potentially contributing to the thermal tolerance and persistence of this invasive mussel.

article.title: Early mitophagy defects and impaired mitochondrial energy metabolism drive target organ damage progression: Lessons from the Fabry heart.
article.authors: Jessica Gambardella; Antonella Fiordelisi; Federica Andrea Cerasuolo; Antonietta Buonaiuto; Roberta Avvisato; Alessandro Viti; Eduardo Sommella; Pietro Campiglia; Valeria D'Argenio; Nella Prevete; Antonio Pezone; Stefania D'Apice; Giovanna Giuseppina Altobelli; Fahimeh Varzideh; Shivangi Pande; Roberta Paolillo; Cinzia Perrino; Eleonora Riccio; Antonio Pisani; Antonio Bianco; Junichi Sadoshima; Letizia Spinelli; Gaetano Santulli; Daniela Sorriento; Guido Iaccarino
article.abstract: Increasing evidence supports a pathogenic role for impaired energy metabolism in organ damage. Genetic diseases provide opportunities to investigate these mechanisms, as exemplified by Fabry disease (FD), caused by an α-galactosidase A (GLA) deficiency and globotriaosylceramide (Gb3) accumulation, with cardiomyopathy as the leading cause of death. Beyond Gb3 storage, impaired energy metabolism may contribute to cardiomyopathy. Here, we demonstrate mitochondrial dysfunction in FD heart and its therapeutic targeting. Using a humanized FD mouse model (R301Q-Tg/GLA knockout), embryonic fibroblasts, and neonatal and adult cardiomyocytes, we found impaired mitophagy and mitochondrial respiration, increased reactive oxygen species, and a vicious cycle aggravating lysosomal dysfunction. These defects progressed with age, causing accumulation of dysfunctional mitochondria, energetic failure, apoptosis, cardiac hypertrophy, and diastolic dysfunction. L-arginine, promoting NO/PGC-1α-dependent mitochondrial rescue, prevented cardiac abnormalities. Our findings identify mitochondrial dysfunction as a key driver of FD cardiomyopathy and reveal the lysosome-mitochondria axis as a targetable pathway in FD and beyond.

article.title: CCN1-mediated stress signaling underlies intrinsic cardiomyocyte dysfunction in spinal muscular atrophy.
article.authors: Wenshu Zeng; Wenqiang Liu; Arianne Caudal; Lichao Liu; Xiaohui Kong; Wenjuan Zhu; Hyeonyu Kim; Aebby Lee; Christina Alamana; Juan Melesio; Xu Cao; Kelly Howell; Karen S Chen; Paul D Pang; John W Day; Joseph C Wu
article.abstract: Cardiac involvement in spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is increasingly recognized, but its cellular basis remains poorly defined. Using patient-specific induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) and engineered heart tissues (EHTs), we identify reduced survival motor neuron (SMN) expression, mitochondrial respiratory defects, and impaired contractility in SMA. Transcriptomic analyses reveal cellular communication network factor 1 (CCN1) as a top upregulated gene in SMA iPSC-CMs, consistent with its enrichment in cardiomyocytes across cardiomyopathies. Exogenous CCN1 exacerbates contractile dysfunction in SMA iPSC-CMs. Proteomic profiling reveals sustained p38/mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling activation, synergistically amplified by CCN1 and TNFα, thereby linking stress signaling to cardiac dysfunction in SMA. Therapeutic intervention with tanshinone IIA suppresses CCN1 expression, attenuates p38 activation, and improves contractile function. Notably, combining tanshinone IIA with risdiplam produces additive benefits in mitochondrial and contractile performance. Together, these findings identify a CCN1-mediated mechanism underlying SMA cardiac dysfunction and support combination strategies integrating SMN-dependent and independent therapies.

article.title: Affective Reserve: Expanding Reserve Theory Beyond Cognition.
article.authors: Elisa Di Rosa
article.abstract: If cognitive systems can build reserve, why should affective systems not do the same? Despite decades of research on brain reserve and cognitive reserve, substantial interindividual variability in affective and cognitive trajectories across the lifespan remains unexplained. Building on the original conceptualization of affective reserve (AR), the present paper further develops AR as a distinct reserve mechanism that extends reserve theory beyond cognition to affective functioning. AR is proposed as a higher-order capacity built and strengthened across the lifespan through the engagement in meaningful and adaptive life experiences that promote the development and the employment of adaptive coping and emotion regulation strategies, and that may involve supportive social relationships. AR is proposed as a higher-order capacity built and strengthened across the lifespan through engagement in meaningful and adaptive life experiences that promote the development and employment of adaptive coping and emotion regulation strategies, and that may involve supportive social relationships. Therefore, AR is hypothesized to constitute an integrated and cumulative affective resource that contributes to resilience and helps explain individual differences in mental health trajectories, beyond what can be explained by cognitive reserve. Given the interdependence of affective and cognitive systems, AR may indeed contribute to both affective and cognitive trajectories and potentially influence the clinical expression of age-related neuropathology and dementia. The present framework specifies the developmental basis and conceptual boundaries of AR, distinguishing it from related constructs including cognitive reserve, emotional reserve, motivational reserve, emotional intelligence, and resilience, and derives testable predictions for future empirical research. By extending reserve theory from cognition to affective functioning, this framework provides a basis for investigating whether cumulative affective system adaptability might represent a previously underexplored source of interindividual variability in mental health, aging, and brain health.

article.title: Integrated microbiome and metabolomic profiling reveals alterations across the adenoma-colorectal cancer sequence.
article.authors: Tien-En Chang; Hung-Hsin Lin; Jiing-Chyuan Luo; Ying-Fan Chen; Yen-Po Wang; Kuei-Chuan Lee; Pei-Chang Lee; Yi-Tsung Lin; Hui-Chun Huang; Chien-Wei Su; Yi-Hsiang Huang; Ming-Chih Hou
article.abstract: The incidence of colorectal cancer (CRC) has been increasing in Taiwan and is associated with multiple risk factors. Increasing evidence suggests that gut microbiota dysbiosis contributes to CRC development. This study aimed to characterize microbial and metabolic alterations across premalignant and malignant colorectal lesions and to identify potential microbiome-associated biomarkers. Individuals undergoing colonoscopy for screening or surveillance at Taipei Veterans General Hospital were enrolled. Gut microbial composition was analyzed using full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing to achieve high-resolution taxonomic profiling. Predicted functional pathways were inferred from microbial communities, and targeted metabolomic profiling was performed to evaluate microbial metabolic outputs. A total of 122 individuals were included, comprising 62 healthy controls, 15 adenoma cases, and 45 CRC cases. Change in microbial composition and predicted functional pathways were observed across the control, adenoma, and CRC groups. Control-associated taxa were linked to carbohydrate fermentation and amino acid metabolism pathways, whereas CRC-associated taxa, particularly Fusobacterium, showed broad negative correlations with multiple biosynthetic pathways. Metabolomic analysis showed increased tauro-ursocholanic acid and reduced short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in CRC. CRC-associated bacteria were negatively correlated with SCFAs and positively correlated with several bile acid metabolites, including lithocholic acid, murocholic acid, tauro-ursocholanic acid, and taurohyocholic acid. Integrative analysis of full-length 16S rRNA sequencing, predicted functional pathways, and metabolomic profiling identified microbial and metabolic differences across the control, adenoma, and CRC groups. These findings are consistent with an association between gut microbial alterations and colorectal neoplasia and may inform future studies of microbial and metabolic biomarkers for CRC.IMPORTANCEColorectal cancer (CRC) develops through an adenoma-carcinoma sequence, yet the microbial and metabolic alterations accompanying this progression remain incompletely understood. In this study, we integrated full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing with metabolomic profiling to characterize taxonomic, functional, and metabolic changes across healthy controls, adenoma, and CRC. Our results showed coordinated changes in microbial taxa, predicted metabolic pathways, and fecal metabolites across the control, adenoma, and CRC groups. Control-associated taxa were linked to pathways related to carbohydrate fermentation and amino acid metabolism, whereas CRC-associated taxa, particularly Fusobacterium, showed negative correlations with several biosynthetic pathways. In addition, CRC-associated taxa were associated with reduced short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and increased levels of certain bile acid-related metabolites. These findings suggest an association between microbiome-associated metabolic alterations and colorectal neoplasia and support further investigation of microbial and metabolic biomarkers.

article.title: Cholesterol-activated VapC12 toxin modulates growth and drug susceptibility in Mycobacterium tuberculosis
article.authors: Hashmi, Z.; Singh, S. P.; Talwar, S.; Megta, A.; Srivastava, M.; Sarmadhikari, D.; Babele, P.; Kundu, S.; Sharma, T.; Sharma, C.; Asthana, S.; Krishnan, V.; Pandey, A. K.
article.abstract: Tuberculosis eradication efforts are severely hampered by antimicrobial resistance and bacterial persistence. We previously reported that the VapBC12 toxin antitoxin (TA) system in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M. tuberculosis) regulates disease progression and antibiotic persistence. In this study, we investigated the molecular mechanisms underlying VapC12 dependent modulation of bacterial growth and antibiotic susceptibility. We identified a Cholesterol Recognition Amino acid Consensus (CRAC) motif in the VapC12 toxin that is critical for cholesterol binding and interaction with its cognate antitoxin, VapB12. Heterologous expression of VapC12 in Mycobacterium smegmatis induced toxicity, providing a model to investigate its functional activity. We determined the crystal structure of VapB12 at 1.6 Angstorm resolution and used molecular modelling to predict the VapBC12 complex structure. Structure-function analyses identified specific residues critical for complex assembly and toxin activity. Mechanistically, our findings suggest that cholesterol activates VapC12 by competitively displacing VapB12 from the CRAC motif, thereby restricting M. tuberculosis growth. Finally, we showed that pharmacologically inhibiting VapC12 alleviates cholesterol-mediated growth restriction and enhances antibiotic activity. Collectively, these findings establish a mechanistic link between cholesterol sensing, toxin-antitoxin regulation, and antibiotic susceptibility in M. tuberculosis, highlighting VapC12 as a potential target for therapeutic strategies to combat tuberculosis persistence.
